maria_eng: Heads up — Vanguard reported invoice amounts off after we merged their customer finetune late yesterday. Quick smokepack please, looks like numeric drift when running int4 quantized variant :eyes:
noah_ml: Can you paste a reproducible example? even one prompt + expected vs observed is fine
riley_infra: tagging infra in case it's a serving path + KV-cache mismatch @riley_infra
maria_eng: Minimal repro below. Note: model is vanguard-finetune+adapter (stitch merge).
```
PROMPT: 'Please extract total amount from invoice:
Invoice #12345
Total: $1,200.00
Thanks.'
EXPECTED: 1200.00
POST-MERGE (float32): 1200.00  (ok)
POST-MERGE (int4 quant): 1000.00  <-- wrong, observed on 3/20 canary
```
noah_ml: hmmm. two hypotheses: tokenizer split + decimal normalization, or quantization pushed representation across a token boundary for the numeric phrase. Can you dump tokens and log probs for int4 run?
maria_eng: Pushed token dump from canary (int4):
```
TOKENS: ["Total", ":", " ", "$", "1", ",", "200", ".", "00"]
LOGPROBS: [-0.2, -0.1, -0.01, -0.05, -0.3, -2.1, -0.8, -0.02, -0.01]
OBS_OUTPUT: "$1,000.00"
```
noah_ml: The comma token has very low prob in int4 run (-2.1) — suggests quantized kernel produced different softmax scale. We should run the same prompt on float32 and int8 to compare kernel behavior.
kai_research: Also try running with KV-cache disabled; sometimes merged adapters change prefix conditioning and interact with batching optimizations.
sam_sre: Deploy-bot reported a canary 3/20 for vanguard-finetune-stitch-int4 at 03:12 UTC then fallback at 03:45 when some customers hit discrepant invoices. :thumbsup:
deploy-bot: Canary deploy 3370001200 -> SUCCESS for latency, but ALERT for correctness metrics (invoice-amount-delta > $1 for 7 users).
maria_eng: I ran quick-eval harness locally: `runtest --model vanguard-finetune-stitch --quant int4 --suite invoice-basic --out json`
Quick metrics: exact_match_rate: 0.88, amount_delta_gt_1: 0.12, mean_abs_amount_error: 14.2
noah_ml: Can you also attach the merge diff (adapter weights overlay) — might be a scale mismatch on the last layer norm. If adapter gain is slightly off, quantization rounding can flip tokens.
maria_eng: Uploaded diff snippet to the thread: `diff --git a/adapter.py b/adapter.py
@@ -120,7 +120,7 @@
- self.scale = 0.97
+ self.scale = 0.997
`
noah_ml: That tiny change + int4 dynamic range could explain the comma drop. Plan: 1) run float32 vs int8 vs int4 on the same harness; 2) re-run with adapter scale pinned to 0.97; 3) run tokenizer-only ablation (no adapter).
riley_infra: I'll queue the harness runs on dedicated infra. ETA ~30m for initial sweep (float32/int8/int4, batch size 1, kv-cache on/off).
kai_research: Also suggest running a tiny calibration set (50 invoices) through quant calibration to see sensitivity: `quant-calibrate --model vanguard-finetune-stitch --calib invoices50.json`
maria_eng: Agree. If int4 shows regression and int8 is fine, we consider shipping int8 fallback for customer Vanguard for now while we fix adapter scale and re-quantize.
sam_sre: I'll prepare a temporary routing policy: requests with header `x-cust-id: vanguard` -> route to model:vanguard-finetune-stitch:int8 in region us-west until fix. Want me to open a rollback?
maria_eng: Yes please, enable routing fallback and pause further canaries. Post results here when runs finish. :pray:
riley_infra: Initial run complete (float32/int8/int4) — uploading CSV to console and summary: float32 EM=0.998, int8 EM=0.995, int4 EM=0.876; amount_delta_gt_1: float32 0.0, int8 0.02, int4 0.13
noah_ml: Confirms quant sensitivity. Action items: - Re-pin adapter scale and re-export; - Requantize and run full quickpack (500 cases); - Ship int8 routing for Vanguard; - Add unit test for numeric token stability in our eval suite.
kai_research: I'll draft a small repro test and PR to add numeric-token-stability to `tests/quickpacks/invoice` — will include token-level logprob assertions to catch low-prob splits.
sam_sre: Routing rule applied, will monitor for 4h then we can relax.
maria_eng: Thanks team — filing a short incident note and will coordinate a follow-up sync. :white_check_mark:
